title: Launch Signal Mesh and Deconflict Scheduler for Runtime/Console/API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Multiple concurrent releases (runtime, console, API) cause scheduling collisions, capacity contention on dedicated pools, and confusing downstream customer communications. We need a single operational artifact (launch signal mesh) that coordinates signals across teams and a deconflict scheduler that enforces blackout windows, prioritization, and capacity hedges for cross-product release trains.

Goal: Provide PMs and Eng leads with a lightweight scheduler + signal mesh that can: 1) register planned launch windows, 2) automatically flag collisions, 3) propose deconflict resolutions based on priority/traffic forecasts, and 4) emit machine-readable signals to runtime and console deployment systems to enact throttles or safety holds.

Why now: Increased Dedicated commitments and Private deployments mean higher risk from overlapping launches. Q2 roadmap has three model-impacting runtime rollouts that need coordinated canaries with console and API surface changes.
scope_in_scope: Launch registry UI schema for Console (signals)
Runbook templates for PM/Eng on conflict resolution
scope_out_of_scope: Implementing autoscaler changes in runtime (only signal hooks delivered)
Full enterprise calendar import (CSV import only, no calendar sync)
success_metrics: Reduction in simultaneous high-risk launches by 75%
Mean time to detect launch collision < 2 hours
% of deconflict suggestions accepted by teams >= 60%
No customer-facing incidents attributable to scheduling conflicts for 90 days after launch
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler accepts launch windows and stores signals in central registry
Collision engine surfaces conflicts with suggested resolution in UI and Slack notifications
Signal webhook subscribed by runtime autopolicy and tested in staging
Runbook documented in Confluence with playbook and rollback criteria
E2E test demonstrating a simulated three-way collision resolved by the scheduler
stakeholders: Solutions Eng / Customer Ops: Rachel Gomez
rollout_plan: Week 1: Prototype scheduler backend + simple UI mockups; design review
Week 2: Collision detection + prioritization rules; integration tests with staging runtime
Week 3: Webhook emitter; onboard one pilot team (runtime canaries)
Week 4: Console UI polish, Slack/Email notifications, pilot retro and adjustments
Week 5: Broader rollout to Console and API teams; enable read-only signals in Dedicated staging
Week 6: GA toggle for internal teams; training and runbook distribution
risks: Teams ignore suggested resolutions -> manual escalation overhead
Webhook consumers may not implement backstops in time
Priority algorithm edge cases causing low-confidence suggestions
Timing drift in timezones causing windows to overlap unexpectedly
notes: Decision: use simple priority score (customer impact, release type, reserved capacity) instead of ML for initial launch
Integrations: send signals to /v1/launch-signals endpoint in runtime staging (ENG task)
We will surface conflicts in Console's release calendar and send Slack alerts to #launch-coord channel
